newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Firms sell 6.4 pct Ericsson Brazil stake.
newsitem.headline: Firms sell 6.4 pct Ericsson Brazil stake.

text.p: Brazil's Monteiro Aranha and Bradesco said they sold a 6.4-percent stake in the local unit of Swedan's Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson for 155.25 million reais ($144 million).
An official at Monteiro Aranha said the 2.7 billion preferred shares of Ericsson Telecomunicacoes S.A. were priced Tuesday at 57.50 reais per lot of 1,000 shares.
Of the total, Monteiro owned two billion of the shares while Bradesco owned 700 million.

Both Monteiro and Aranha, who traded their voting stakes in Ericsson for non-voting preferred shares late last year when the firm came under majority control by its Swedish parent, made large premiums on the sale, according to market sources.
Ericsson preferred, which traded late Thursday at 64.10 reais, has risen 300 percent this year and 1,335 percent since early 1996.
The firms traded their voting stakes in the firm for Monteiro officials have said they intend to use the money to invest in cellular phones, electrical energy and water and sewer services, he added.

The share offering was coordinated by Banco Bradesco S.A., Banco Patrimonio de Investimentos S.A., Banco Icatu S.A., Banco de Investimentos Garantia S.A., Indosuez Capital DTVM S.A., Banco InterAtlantico S.A. and Banco Bozano, Simonsen S.A.
In a joint statement, the sale coordinators said that they have five days to place the shares
